svg.text: USB PHY ownership and the boot recovery window
One shared USB PHY, two controllers that fight over it, and the millisecond window that decides whether esptool recovery is reachable.

text.tspan: enumerates as 303A:1001, carries the boot log

svg.text: TinyUSB (device) or the USB host stack
no external mux — one owner at a time
shared internal USB PHY → D-/D+ pads (GPIO19/20) → USB-C J1

text.tspan: Only one can own the pads at a time. The switch is internal to the SoC — there is no external mux. The hand-over happens the moment code calls
usb_new_phy(), which has exactly two callers in the stock image: tinyusb_driver_install (Disk Mode) and usb_host_install (normal-mode keyboard

USJ stays up until power is cut

The boot-mode word lives in RAM only and is never persisted. The CC-role controller plays no part in any of this — its MODE_SELECT register is never
written, so the CC role is strap-fixed and identical in every mode.

0 → 5000 ms since reset. Numbered ticks key to the event list beneath each lane; closely spaced ticks are stacked so none are hidden.
USB-Serial-JTAG owns the PHY — esptool download mode reachable

~62 ms — USJ device enumerates on the host

870–880 ms — Lua UI bundle loaded from the assets
910 ms — CC status read: device is the sink, host is
1020 ms — “checking for update” — the SD updater scan
runs on every boot, before the display is up
1030 ms — backlight initialised and display driver
1040–4080 ms — 3.04 s block of silence: display
bring-up. This one gap is 74% of the window
4140 ms — the hand-over: HID host init →
USJ window held open deliberately: the PHY is handed back to the USB-Serial-JTAG
controller as the third action of boot, and TinyUSB is not started until a
configured minimum uptime (5000 ms as shipped)

svg.text: 0 ms — power latch driven LOW, stock GPIO parity block, PHY handed back to USJ

text.tspan: 5000 ms — TinyUSB claims the USB-OTG PHY; the CDC
link comes up (continues past the edge of this
On this chip a software restart resets neither the RTC sub-system holding the PHY mux nor the USB peripherals. Without the explicit hand-back, any
reboot taken after TinyUSB started would come back with the PHY still on USB-OTG — no console and no esptool recovery until a physical power cycle.
Download mode over USB-Serial-JTAG needs no GPIO0/BOOT pin — esptool has a VID/PID-detected reset strategy that drives it over DTR/RTS, as long as
the USJ peripheral, not the application, owns the pads. That is what this window is for.
